resum: It filed on 26 October under the ticker ANT. The filing shows revenue of $16.3bn in the first half of 2026 (up from $1.2bn a year earlier) and an operating loss of $693m; the founders will keep 50.1% of the votes.
per_que_importa: Once it's listed, anyone will be able to buy its shares, and it would be one of the biggest debuts in history: a test of how far confidence in the AI business really goes.
xifra_text: Anthropic's revenue in the first half of 2026

titular: A Chinese humanoid robot learns to work as a shop assistant in five days
resum: AGIBOT has unveiled GO-3, an AI model for robots. In a test shop, its G2 robot went from completing 28.6% of tasks on day one to 85.7% on day five, without anyone teaching it each step. The company plans to release the model openly by the end of the year.
per_que_importa: Robots no longer need to be programmed task by task: they learn by practising. That could soon bring them into shops and warehouses, with knock-on effects for jobs and productivity.
xifra_text: tasks completed by the robot, from day one to day five

titular: OpenAI in talks to raise $30bn at a $1.25tn valuation
resum: Coatue would lead the round alongside investors from the UAE, according to CNBC sources. OpenAI filed confidentially to go public in June; Anthropic, valued at $965bn in May, is reportedly aiming for $1.5–2tn at its debut.
per_que_importa: AI companies are already worth more than many big listed firms despite earning little or losing money: that's why some people talk of a revolution and others warn of a bubble.
xifra_text: OpenAI's valuation in the round under negotiation

titular: Spanish start-ups have already raised more money than in all of 2025
resum: By September they had raised €3.83bn, 22% more than in the whole of last year, driven by mega-rounds such as Multiverse Computing (€500m) and Open Cosmos (€300m). Barcelona (€1,175m) and Madrid (€1,153m) are almost neck and neck.
per_que_importa: More investment means more new companies hiring and doing research here. But two-thirds of the money went into just 16 deals: without the mega-rounds, investment fell by 8%.
xifra_text: raised by Spanish start-ups through September

titular: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon, for now only for cybersecurity experts
resum: It tops the Artificial Analysis intelligence index with 59 points, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, though only by a few points. There's no date for general access while it goes through the US government's voluntary testing.
per_que_importa: The most powerful models are no longer released to everyone at once: experts and the government test them first, for fear they could be used to attack computer systems.
xifra_text: on the Artificial Analysis intelligence index

titular: Humanoid robots arrive in car factories
resum: Figure has already built more than 350 and tested them at BMW's Spartanburg plant; Mercedes-Benz uses Apptronik's robots to move parts, and Schaeffler wants to install at least 1,000 in its plants within seven years.
per_que_importa: The car industry, a big presence in Catalonia, is the first to try them out: it's where we'll see whether they replace workers or help them with the most repetitive jobs.
xifra_text: robots Schaeffler wants in its plants within seven years

titular: GPT-6.1 Terra: OpenAI's fast, cheap model for getting work done on your computer
resum: It costs $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, half the price of its siblings, and according to OpenAI it completes tasks more than three times faster than GPT-6 Astra. For the most complex coding, OpenAI itself recommends its larger models.
per_que_importa: AI keeps getting cheaper, which means more companies adopt it and the tools you use every day come with it built in.

titular: Claude Enterprise shows companies what their AI spending is getting them
resum: New per-team reports, surveys and shared budgets. According to Jellyfish data, spending on Claude-based tools has grown tenfold since January and already accounts for almost a third of code changes submitted for review.
per_que_importa: Companies no longer want to spend on AI blindly: they want to know what they get for it. It's the shift from hype to productivity you can measure.
xifra_text: spending on Claude-based tools since January, according to Jellyfish

titular: Alphabet plunges despite Google Cloud's strong run
resum: Third-quarter revenue of $127.58bn came in just below forecasts, and on Thursday the stock had the worst session in its history (−12.6%). Google Cloud brought in $30.7bn.
per_que_importa: Not even the giants are safe: if AI investment doesn't pay off soon enough, the market punishes them.

titular: Mistral releases open weights for Large 4, a trillion-parameter model
resum: The French company, Europe's big bet in AI, is aiming it at coding and defensive cybersecurity.
per_que_importa: Europe having its own open models means not relying solely on US or Chinese companies for a key technology.

titular: Canada takes a stake in Cohere worth up to C$1.6bn
resum: In return, the company must keep its headquarters in the country and invest at least C$1.7bn there in computing capacity before 2030.
per_que_importa: Governments are starting to treat AI as a strategic sector, just like energy: they want homegrown companies and don't want to depend on others.
